lesson_card.plain_english: every tool, server, connector, and permission an agent can touch becomes a new place for risk
lesson_card.big_question: If an AI agent can touch more tools, does that make it more useful or more dangerous?
lesson_card.simple_analogy: giving an intern keys to every room in the building and then acting surprised when a door opens
lesson_card.common_misunderstanding: People focus on the launch. The useful question is who gains control, who inherits risk, and what changes tomorrow.
lesson_card.hard_receipt: The provided story snippet is thin on hard numbers; the honest move is to say that and analyze consequence.
lesson_card.listener_payoff: By the end, listeners should understand agent surface area well enough to explain why today's AI story matters tomorrow.
lesson_card.operator_lesson: Do not ask only what launched. Ask what new permission, risk, cost, or accountability chain just appeared.
lesson_card.episode_spine: Bessent says the U.S. proposed an AI incident alert system in China talks shows that every new agent connector also creates a new place for risk.
